raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Offline pooling (`LLM.encode`, `embed`, `classify`, `score`) already feeds the engine incrementally, but it preprocessed the entire prompt list before adding the first request, so the GPU sat idle for the whole preprocessing phase. This makes the offline request factory lazy and replaces the eager `Executor.map` in `_run_tiling_engine` with a bounded prefetch, so the first requests reach the engine after a bounded amount of preprocessing instead of all of it.

Independent of the multi-item scoring RFC and of the other pooling PRs in this series; it applies to any offline pooling call.

## Claims

- The engine receives its first requests after at most `2 * max_num_seqs` prompts have been preprocessed, instead of after all of them.
- GPU utilization at the start of a large offline pooling call (`LLM.encode`, `embed`, ...) rises earlier; the larger the prompt list (and the larger the per-request `PoolingParams`), the longer the idle window that is removed.
- Outputs are unchanged: same values, same order.
- No Python API change. The only caller-visible difference is *when* a malformed prompt is reported: an error from `parse_model_prompt` now surfaces when that prompt is reached rather than before the first request is added. The existing abort-on-exception path in `_run_tiling_engine` already aborts whatever was added before the failure; a test now pins that.

## Validation

Environment: 1x H100 80GB, vLLM main @ 2d40c0609f (nightly wheel), torch 2.14.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`).

### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py \
       tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py \
       tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py \
       tests/entrypoints/pooling/basic/test_tiling_engine.py
# all passed; test_io_processor.py 11 (main: 8, the three new unit tests),
# token_embed/test_late_chunking.py 36 and basic/test_tiling_engine.py 4, same as main

pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
# exit 0
```

Every test file under `tests/entrypoints/pooling` that does not start an API server — 21 files, covering embed, classify, token-classify, token-embed, the scoring bi-encoder / cross-encoder / late-interaction suites — was run per file on this branch and on unpatched main on the same host, with identical results apart from the three new tests: 19 files pass fully on both with identical counts, and the remaining failures occur on both builds and are environment-only (`token_embed/test_offline.py` 2 failed, the bge-m3 and nomic checkpoints are not available offline on that host; `scoring/test_late_interaction_offline_vision.py` 3 errors, model not cached offline). So no regression. The API-server tests (`*_online*.py`, `test_truncation.py`, the mteb correctness tests) were not run: the change is in the offline `LLM` path only (`get_request_factory_offline`, `_run_tiling_engine`), which the server does not use, and the host has no network to start them.

Three unit tests are added to `tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_io_processor.py`, which runs on CPU with a stubbed engine and needs no model:

- the engine receives its first `add_request` after at most `2 * max_num_seqs` items have been produced by the request factory, while the full list is 1,000 prompts, and all outputs still come back in request order;
- a request factory that fails partway through propagates the error and the requests already added to the engine are aborted;
- the caller's `PoolingParams` object is not mutated — the yielded requests carry the pooling task, the caller's object keeps `task is None`.

The file is already covered by the existing Buildkite entrypoints job, so no CI configuration change is needed. The benchmark below was run by hand and is not part of CI.

### Benchmark

Workload: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`, one `LLM.embed` call with 20,000 synthetic token-id prompts of 200-400 tokens (uniform), on 1 GPU, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, `max_model_len=1024`, prefix caching off. One untimed warmup call, then 3 timed calls; two separate runs per branch. GPU utilization sampled with `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu -lms 50`.

| Metric | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| per-call wall time, run 1 / run 2 | 16.11 / 16.92 / 16.64 s and 16.15 / 17.37 / 16.46 s | 15.41 / 16.27 / 15.62 s and 15.36 / 15.71 / 16.14 s |
| median call time | 16.55 s | 15.67 s |
| prompts/s | 1,151-1,242 | 1,229-1,302 |
| GPU utilization in the first second of a call | 0-3% | 14-60% |

That is **+5.6% throughput** on the medians; comparing the same call index between branches, the individual calls are +2% to +11% faster.

Output check: the embeddings are identical to main within main's own run-to-run variation — max |diff| 0.0 in one run and 3.0e-8 in 1 of 20,000 rows in the other, which is exactly what two main runs differ by.

## Details

**Lazy offline request factory.** `PoolingIOProcessor.get_request_factory_offline` used to run `parse_model_prompt` over every prompt and `PoolingParams.clone()` over every parameter object in two list comprehensions, then return a generator over the already-built lists. Both moves into the generator, one request per `yield`. The validation that must still fail before anything is added — a request whose `PoolingParams.task` conflicts with the model's pooling task, with the existing `plugin` exception — stays up front; it only reads the uncloned parameters and does not touch the prompts, so it is cheap. The caller's parameters are still never mutated: the clone now happens inside the generator, just before the task is filled in.

The other `get_request_factory_offline` implementations were checked. The cross-encoder scoring factory (`ScoringIOProcessor`) is already lazy and is untouched. The bi-encoder scoring, Jina ranking and token-embed factories delegate to the base one and become lazy with it. The `IOProcessorPlugin` factory still clones and merges parameters eagerly before delegating, because a plugin's `pre_process` has to produce the whole prompt list anyway; its eager clone is left alone.

**Bounded prefetch instead of `Executor.map`.** `_run_tiling_engine` called `self._executor.map(io_processor.render, request_factory())`. `concurrent.futures.Executor.map` submits every item of the iterable when it is called — Python before 3.14 has no `buffersize` parameter — so it drained the generator up front and undid the laziness above. It is replaced by a deque of render futures that is topped up to `max_requests_in_core` (`2 * max_num_seqs`, the number of requests the loop is about to add) at the top of each loop iteration and consumed in order. Rendering therefore still overlaps with the engine's steps, but never runs more than one batch ahead; output order and the exception behaviour are unchanged, and any futures left pending when the loop exits are cancelled.

I chose the bounded version rather than the lazy `map(io_processor.render, request_factory())` fallback because the latter would render on the calling thread, serializing preprocessing with the engine loop and giving up the overlap the thread pool exists for; the bounded version is only a few lines and keeps both properties.

### Duplicate check

Searched open vLLM PRs on 2026-10-21 with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` for "offline pooling preprocessing", "get_request_factory_offline" and "pooling lazy encode". Nothing open changes the offline pooling request factory or the `Executor.map` call. The closest open PR is #54771, which bulk-submits an already-built offline request group over a single engine-core message to avoid microbatch fragmentation; it addresses how requests are handed to the engine core, not when they are built, and the two are complementary.
#48544 speeds up tokenization of offline prompts, which is a different stage and does not make the
factory lazy.

The code, tests and this description were written with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot). I reviewed every changed line; the tests and benchmarks listed above were run on the hardware described.

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

🔴 Two existing late-chunking unit tests will fail in CI with `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'submit'`. They pass on the base branch. `_run_tiling_engine` now calls `self._executor.submit` (offline.py:449). The test stub at tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py:217 sets `llm._executor = SimpleNamespace(map=map)`, so it has no `submit`. Fix: update `_mock_chunk_llm` to give the stub a `submit`, for example an inline Executor like the `_InlineExecutor` added in test_io_processor.py. Then both tests that use it reach their `step` and row-count assertions again.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

`_mock_chunk_llm` (tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py:210-227) binds the real `PoolingOfflineMixin._run_tiling_engine`. It replaces the executor with `SimpleNamespace(map=map)` (line 217), which only matched the old `self._executor.map(io_processor.render, request_factory())` call. After this change, the first loop iteration calls `prefetch()`, and `prefetch()` runs `self._executor.submit(io_processor.render, request)` (offline.py:449). That raises AttributeError before any request is added. `test_late_chunk_mapping_preserves_order_mixed_requests_and_errors` (line 241) wraps the call in `pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="step failed")`, which does not catch AttributeError, so the test fails. `test_late_chunk_mapping_rejects_successful_output_with_wrong_row_count` (line 280) expects `ValueError, match="does not match"` and fails the same way. On the base branch both pass because `map` exists on the stub. The PR's validation section only ran test_io_processor.py and test_factories.py, so it never hit this file, but the Buildkite entrypoints job will.

**Verification:** In tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py, `_mock_chunk_llm` stubs the executor with `llm._executor = SimpleNamespace(map=map)` (line 217), and that stub has no `submit`. `prefetch()` runs `self._executor.submit(io_processor.render, request)` (offline.py:449), which raises AttributeError. On the base, `self._executor.map` worked with the builtin `map`.

</details>

nodes.body:
Thank you for the question — you are right for text prompts, and I measured it.

1x H100 80GB, `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` bf16, one `LLM.embed` call with 20,000 prompts of
200-400 tokens, 3 timed calls after a warmup:

| input | main mean | this PR mean | change | GPU util, seconds 1/2/3 (main → this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| text, 2 runs x 3 calls | 22.8 s | 23.1 s | -1%, within noise | 0/0/0-9% → 0/0/58-69% |
| token ids, 1 run x 3 calls | 16.7 s | 15.9 s | +4.5% | 0/22-83/84-86% → 55-63/85-89/84-90% |

On main, `Executor.map` submits every render up front, so the thread pool tokenizes continuously;
this PR renders at most `max_requests_in_core` ahead. The GPU starts about a second earlier, but
fewer renders are in flight in steady state, and the two effects cancel. The gain only shows with
pre-tokenized input, where rendering is cheap and main's serial up-front phase dominates.

Since the gain is limited to pre-tokenized input and the change adds complexity, I am closing this
PR; thanks again for the question.

@@ -1,11 +1,12 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 
+from concurrent.futures import Executor, Future
 from types import SimpleNamespace
 
 import pytest
 
-from vllm import PoolingParams
+from vllm import PoolingParams, PoolingRequestOutput
 from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.base.io_processor import PoolingIOProcessor
 from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.offline import PoolingOfflineMixin
 from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.scoring.io_processor import CrossEncoderIOProcessor
@@ -258,3 +259,163 @@ def test_score_leaves_caller_pooling_params_untouched(monkeypatch):
         "PoolingParams; reusing that object with another pooling model now "
         "fails with 'You cannot overwrite ...' before any inference runs."
     )
+
+
+class _InlineExecutor(Executor):
+    """Executor that renders on the calling thread, for deterministic tests."""
+
+    def submit(self, fn, /, *args, **kwargs):
+        future: Future = Future()
+        try:
+            future.set_result(fn(*args, **kwargs))
+        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            future.set_exception(exc)
+        return future
+
+
+class _FakeEngine:
+    """Engine that finishes one request per step, in arrival order."""
+
+    def __init__(self, max_num_seqs: int):
+        self.vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(
+            scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(max_num_seqs=max_num_seqs)
+        )
+        self.in_core: list[str] = []
+        self.aborted: list[str] = []
+        self.num_added = 0
+
+    def has_unfinished_requests(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self.in_core)
+
+    def step(self) -> list[PoolingRequestOutput]:
+        if not self.in_core:
+            return []
+        request_id = self.in_core.pop(0)
+        return [
+            PoolingRequestOutput(
+                request_id=request_id,
+                outputs=None,
+                prompt_token_ids=[],
+                num_cached_tokens=0,
+                finished=True,
+            )
+        ]
+
+    def abort_request(self, request_ids) -> None:
+        self.aborted.extend(request_ids)
+
+
+def _make_tiling_llm(
+    monkeypatch,
+    engine: _FakeEngine,
+    on_add=None,
+) -> PoolingOfflineMixin:
+    """A pooling LLM whose engine and rendering are stubbed out.
+
+    `_run_tiling_engine` runs for real so that the interleaving between
+    preprocessing and `add_request` is observable.
+    """
+    llm = PoolingOfflineMixin.__new__(PoolingOfflineMixin)
+    llm.llm_engine = engine
+    monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "_executor", _InlineExecutor(), raising=False)
+
+    def render_and_add_requests(prompts, params, lora_requests, priorities):

🔴 Two existing late-chunking unit tests will fail in CI with `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'submit'`. They pass on the base branch. `_run_tiling_engine` now calls `self._executor.submit` (offline.py:449). The test stub at tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py:217 sets `llm._executor = SimpleNamespace(map=map)`, so it has no `submit`. Fix: update `_mock_chunk_llm` to give the stub a `submit`, for example an inline Executor like the `_InlineExecutor` added in test_io_processor.py. Then both tests that use it reach their `step` and row-count assertions again.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

`_mock_chunk_llm` (tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py:210-227) binds the real `PoolingOfflineMixin._run_tiling_engine`. It replaces the executor with `SimpleNamespace(map=map)` (line 217), which only matched the old `self._executor.map(io_processor.render, request_factory())` call. After this change, the first loop iteration calls `prefetch()`, and `prefetch()` runs `self._executor.submit(io_processor.render, request)` (offline.py:449). That raises AttributeError before any request is added. `test_late_chunk_mapping_preserves_order_mixed_requests_and_errors` (line 241) wraps the call in `pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="step failed")`, which does not catch AttributeError, so the test fails. `test_late_chunk_mapping_rejects_successful_output_with_wrong_row_count` (line 280) expects `ValueError, match="does not match"` and fails the same way. On the base branch both pass because `map` exists on the stub. The PR's validation section only ran test_io_processor.py and test_factories.py, so it never hit this file, but the Buildkite entrypoints job will.

**Verification:** In tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py, `_mock_chunk_llm` stubs the executor with `llm._executor = SimpleNamespace(map=map)` (line 217), and that stub has no `submit`. `prefetch()` runs `self._executor.submit(io_processor.render, request)` (offline.py:449), which raises AttributeError. On the base, `self._executor.map` worked with the builtin `map`.

</details>

Thank you for the question — you are right for text prompts, and I measured it.

1x H100 80GB, `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` bf16, one `LLM.embed` call with 20,000 prompts of
200-400 tokens, 3 timed calls after a warmup:

| input | main mean | this PR mean | change | GPU util, seconds 1/2/3 (main → this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| text, 2 runs x 3 calls | 22.8 s | 23.1 s | -1%, within noise | 0/0/0-9% → 0/0/58-69% |
| token ids, 1 run x 3 calls | 16.7 s | 15.9 s | +4.5% | 0/22-83/84-86% → 55-63/85-89/84-90% |

On main, `Executor.map` submits every render up front, so the thread pool tokenizes continuously;
this PR renders at most `max_requests_in_core` ahead. The GPU starts about a second earlier, but
fewer renders are in flight in steady state, and the two effects cancel. The gain only shows with
pre-tokenized input, where rendering is cheap and main's serial up-front phase dominates.

Since the gain is limited to pre-tokenized input and the change adds complexity, I am closing this
PR; thanks again for the question.
